## Tours to Laguna Capri: a short hike within a grand Patagonia itinerary

[Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/) lies near [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) in the northern part of [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/). A trail through Patagonian forest leads to its shore, where the Fitz Roy massif is visible unless the peaks are hidden by clouds. It is a good introduction to local mountain trails without a long day's hike to the mountain's base.

Our catalog lists {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} including Laguna Capri among the main destinations. **When choosing a trip, the lagoon's place in the schedule matters as much as its name.** A short hike after a transfer, a separate full day in the mountains and an extended trek require different levels of stamina.

You can choose a ready-made tour here. For a separate description of the shoreline and scenery, see the [Laguna Capri destination page](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/).

## Where Laguna Capri features in Ada Tours itineraries

On the [13-day Argentina, Chile and Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/), the visit to Capri takes place on **day 7**. Participants first travel from [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) to El Chaltén. After arrival, they begin the half-day hike to the lagoon.

The trail climbs away from the village toward views of the Las Vueltas River valley, then reaches viewpoints of Fitz Roy and a branch leading to Capri's shore. Most of the return path is downhill. This is a rewarding mountain walk but considerably shorter than the route to [Laguna de los Tres](/argentina/place/laguna-de-los-tres/).

The logic of the itinerary is simple: after a day of travel, you can get onto a trail and see the mountains without planning a long ascent until dark. **The following day, day 8, involves a full trekking excursion.** It is worth considering the combined effort of both days, particularly if you rarely walk on uneven ground.

## How Laguna Capri fits into the rest of the 13-day trip

The [Argentina and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) begins in Buenos Aires. Next comes Tierra del Fuego, including Ushuaia and lakes Fagnano and Escondido; near El Calafate, travelers visit [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). Then follow two different hiking days around El Chaltén.

Day 7 is a **half-day hike to Laguna Capri after the transfer**. Day 8 takes the group through the forest and Poincenot area toward Laguna de los Tres; the final steep climb to the lake is offered to participants ready for the extra exertion. The itinerary then crosses into Chile and continues through Puerto Natales, Torres del Paine and Santiago.

This journey suits people wanting to combine southern Argentina's natural landscapes with Chilean Patagonia and a city finale. **The two hiking days in El Chaltén are an important part of the trip**, not just a quick stop to photograph Fitz Roy.

## Laguna Capri or Laguna de los Tres: what's the difference?

Both destinations are associated with the Fitz Roy massif, but they differ in time and effort. According to Argentine government tourism information, the classic route from El Chaltén to **Capri is about 8 km round trip**, while the full route to **Laguna de los Tres is approximately 25 km round trip** and is more demanding. These distances apply to common trails starting in the village; individual approaches may differ.

| Criterion | Capri / De los Tres |
|---|---|
| Time required | Half a day / full day |
| Main effort | Forest trail with an ascent / long hike with a steep final section |
| Main highlight | Fitz Roy views from the shore / lake at the foot of the mountains |

**You do not have to complete the long Laguna de los Tres route to visit Capri.** It is a destination in its own right. On Ada Tours' 13-day trip, the two places fall on separate days, allowing travelers to view the Fitz Roy area from a lower vantage point and during the following longer hike.

If you are chiefly interested in major hiking routes, also browse [adventure journeys](/interests/adventure/) and read their itineraries carefully rather than choosing only by photographs of mountains.

## Assessing physical demands before departure

Although the trail to Capri is relatively short, it is a mountain path with ascents, descents and rocky or wet sections. A trip with a short trek will not necessarily suit someone expecting a stroll on a level path. Sturdy, grippy walking shoes and waterproof outerwear are far more useful here than city footwear.

Patagonian wind and weather can change quickly. Views of Fitz Roy are not guaranteed, even in good weather down in El Chaltén. Bring water, a snack and an additional warm layer. Remember the return journey when dressing: after a stop by the lake, your body cools faster.

For this particular program, assess **the combined demands of days 7 and 8** in advance. The first outing is relatively short but follows a transfer. The next day's route is longer, and the final ascent to Laguna de los Tres requires additional effort. Participants uncertain of their fitness should discuss this part before booking.

## When to plan the walk to Capri

The southern summer, when daylight hours are longer, is usually the most convenient period for independent hiking in the area. However, clear mountain panoramas depend on cloud and wind, and precipitation is possible even in the warmer months. Consider the conditions on the specific date rather than treating any season as a guarantee of good visibility.

Avoid crowding the walking day with additional trips. After arriving from El Calafate, leave realistic time to change clothes, start the hike, stop by the water and return to the village. The 13-day program reflects this balance by choosing a half-day route, but the pace always depends on the group and trail conditions.

## Questions about tours through Laguna Capri

### How far is Laguna Capri from El Chaltén on foot?

Official Argentine tourism materials give **approximately 8 km round trip** for the usual route. Allowing half a day works well. Actual duration depends on pace, stops and trail conditions.

### Is Laguna Capri included in the 13-day tour or offered as an extra?

It is part of **day 7** of the [Argentina, Chile and Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) after arrival in El Chaltén. This is one of the program's planned hiking days.

### Must I trek all the way to Laguna de los Tres to see Capri?

No. [Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/) is a separate destination reached on a shorter walk. [Laguna de los Tres](/argentina/place/laguna-de-los-tres/) requires a much longer and more physically challenging hike.

### Can I see Fitz Roy without the difficult final ascent?

Yes. When visibility is good, the Fitz Roy massif can already be seen from Laguna Capri and the viewpoints on its approach. This makes the shorter walk suitable for travelers who value the mountain panorama more than reaching the higher glacial lake.

### What if the forecast predicts strong winds?

The decision to hike depends on actual trail conditions and park administration recommendations. Strong winds can make even a familiar route unpleasant or unsafe. On a tour with several hiking days, discuss changes with the organizer and guide rather than assuming transfers or substitutions not included in the program.

## Laguna de los Tres: a challenging trek to the foot of Fitz Roy

Laguna de los Tres lies in Argentine Patagonia near [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/). Sharp granite peaks of the Fitz Roy massif rise above its cold waters, with glacial slopes visible nearby. This is one of the best-known walking routes in Los Glaciares National Park.

The defining feature of the trek is the gradual transition from forest and river valleys to exposed rocky slopes. The final ascent toward the lake is usually the most difficult section. So the useful question before setting out is whether participants have the strength and time for the way back after the climb, not just the desire to see the famous view.

## Trail length and the final climb

According to Argentina's tourism authority, the classic route from El Chaltén to Laguna de los Tres is about **25 km round trip**, usually requiring **8–9 hours**. The national park guide classifies it as a moderate to difficult trail. These figures apply to a common version of the route; distances and itinerary change when starting elsewhere.

Initially, the path leads through forest and viewpoints over the valley. More exposed sections with mountain views follow. The last ascent is unlike the earlier stretches: the ground is rocky, the grade is steep and the group's pace slows. Wind, wet rocks or snow can make this section considerably harder.

Our [13-day Argentina and Chile journey](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) uses a different start: participants are driven to the El Pilar hostería, then follow a trail through forest and the Río Blanco area. The final ascent to Laguna de los Tres involves gaining approximately 500 m of elevation. After visiting the lake, the return route passes through the [Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/) area. These details belong to that specific program; not every visitor begins at El Pilar.

## Capri or De los Tres: which should you choose?

| Criterion | Where to go |
|---|---|
| Half-day walk | [Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/) |
| Full mountain day | Laguna de los Tres |
| Lower physical demands | [Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/) |
| Closer to Fitz Roy | Laguna de los Tres |

[Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/) offers views of Fitz Roy from the forest zone and a chance to finish earlier. Laguna de los Tres suits travelers prepared for extended walking and a steep final ascent. Views of the peaks depend on clouds at both places, so embarking on the longer route for a single photograph is a gamble.

If a participant is tired before the final climb, it is wiser to consider a safe return or an alternative rest point. Route planning should account for the fitness of the slowest person in the group.

## When to go and what equipment to bring

In the Southern Hemisphere's warm months, the trek is generally more accessible, but Patagonian weather is changeable all year. Strong winds, precipitation and lingering snow on exposed sections can increase the difficulty considerably. Check current warnings and trail conditions before setting out, and start early enough to return in daylight.

For a long trekking day, bring broken-in boots with good grip, wind and rain protection, a warm layer, and sufficient water and food. Allow time for rest and photography. Do not start this route with unsuitable footwear or assume that the way back will be free of fatigue.

Registration requirements, national park access rules and weather restrictions can change. Before departure, check the official Los Glaciares rules and the terms of your chosen guiding arrangement.

## Frequently asked questions about Laguna de los Tres

### How long does the hike take?

The classic route from El Chaltén usually takes 8–9 hours and is approximately 25 km round trip. Starting elsewhere can change those figures.

### Is De los Tres harder than Laguna Capri?

Yes. [Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/) is a shorter hike, while De los Tres requires a full day and a steep final climb.

### Can I see Fitz Roy without completing the last ascent?

Yes. The massif is visible from earlier sections of the trail, including [Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/). The final climb to the lake is for those who want to get closer to the foot of the mountains.

### Is this trail included in an Ada Tours trip?

We include this trail as a separate trekking day on the [Argentina, Chile and Patagonia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/). Check the specific tour description for guiding, transfers and route details.

## Tours to Laguna de los Tres: a route to the foot of Fitz Roy

[Laguna de los Tres](/argentina/place/laguna-de-los-tres/) lies in Argentine Patagonia in the northern part of [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/). Sharp granite peaks of the Fitz Roy massif rise above the glacial lake. Travelers come to [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) for this view and devote a full day to the mountain trail.

Our catalog lists {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} including Laguna de los Tres in their main geographic route. But **listing the lake among the stops** and **actually ascending to its shore** are different things. The current Ada Tours program includes a long hiking day, while the guide offers the final steep section to the lagoon to participants ready for the extra exertion. This matters for expectations and preparation.

Learn more about the geography, natural features and lake views on the [Laguna de los Tres destination page](/argentina/place/laguna-de-los-tres/). Here, the focus is the tour's content and how to complete the day within your capabilities.

## How the Laguna de los Tres day works on an Ada Tours trip

On the [13-day Argentina, Chile and Patagonia journey](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/), the hike takes place on **day 8**. The day before, the group arrives in El Chaltén and takes a shorter walk to [Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/). The following day, the route is longer, with views of Fitz Roy gradually opening from different points.

### Starting near El Pilar hostería

In the morning, a minibus transfers the group to the trailhead near the El Pilar hostería, around 18 km from El Chaltén. This matters: the program **does not completely follow the classic out-and-back route starting in the village**. According to the itinerary, the trail runs through lenga and ñire forests alongside the Río Blanco.

The first part of the day includes viewpoints, including a view of Piedras Blancas Glacier. The route then reaches the Poincenot camping area, from which it continues toward Río Blanco base camp. Even without the final ascent, this is already a substantial mountain hike.

### Final ascent and return

The guide offers fit participants the option to make the more demanding ascent to Laguna de los Tres. The concluding section involves about **500 m of elevation gain**. This steep portion is physically harder than the earlier walking through forest. At the shore, the celebrated panorama of Fitz Roy, neighboring peaks and glaciers unfolds if weather permits.

After a rest, the group returns to El Chaltén. According to the itinerary, the return follows the [Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/) viewpoint. Thus the two days introduce travelers to the same mountain area from different angles: first a half-day lake walk, then a major route toward the foot of the massif.

| Part of the day | What's planned |
|---|---|
| Start | Transfer to El Pilar |
| Main trail | Forest, Piedras Blancas, Poincenot |
| Final section | Steep climb for those ready |
| Return | Via the Capri viewpoint |

## How difficult is the trek and how long does it take?

Official Argentine tourism materials classify the classic Laguna de los Tres hike as **moderate to difficult**; the common route from El Chaltén is around **25 km round trip**. The park administration advises a full day, approximately 8–9 hours. These figures apply to the usual trail from the village and **must not be applied mechanically to the El Pilar start** used by Ada Tours.

Starting from El Pilar changes the approach to the lake but not the long walk or the demanding final section. Duration depends on the group's pace, trail conditions, breaks and whether participants undertake the final climb. Treating it as an ordinary walk to a lookout would be misleading.

Take particular care when assessing **the final elevation gain on the rocky path**. After several hours of walking, climbing becomes harder. Two consecutive mountain days may be tiring for someone unused to long walks on uneven terrain.

## How this program differs from a standalone trip to El Chaltén

Laguna de los Tres on the Ada Tours itinerary is part of an extended journey through Argentina and Chile. Before reaching the mountain trails, participants have visited Buenos Aires, Tierra del Fuego and [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). After El Chaltén, the route continues through Chile's Puerto Natales, Torres del Paine and Santiago.

This format suits travelers who want to experience **different natural regions in a single journey**, with hiking as an important element. On a separate visit to El Chaltén, you can allow more spare days for poor weather or alternate strenuous hikes with rest. The 13-day itinerary does not include dedicated contingency days for Laguna de los Tres.

If the main aim is one specific Fitz Roy view, consider the possibility of low cloud. Even on a well-organized trek, the peaks can remain hidden. This is a real limitation for a journey with a fixed sequence of cities and flights.

## Capri and De los Tres: two different hiking days

[Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/) offers a shorter introduction to the Fitz Roy area: official sources give approximately 8 km round trip on the usual trail from El Chaltén. This route provides views of the massif and wooded shores without the long final climb.

[Laguna de los Tres](/argentina/place/laguna-de-los-tres/) takes much more time and effort. These destinations should be seen as **different challenges**, not interchangeable photographic stops. On the [13-day tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/), Capri is planned for day 7 and the longer trek for day 8.

For a broader search for mountain trips, compare [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) and [adventure programs](/interests/adventure/). Base any decision about effort on the actual daily itinerary.

## What to prepare and when to go

This trek requires broken-in footwear with good grip, several clothing layers, rain and wind protection, water and a snack. Weather can change in a single day. Wind is more noticeable on the exposed final section, and a break by the lake can cool you quickly.

The southern summer with its long days is a popular choice for hiking in this area. However, the date itself does not guarantee safe passage or views of the peaks. Before departure, check the national park's current trail and weather notices. Decide whether to continue on the steep final stretch according to real conditions and participants' capabilities.

On the Ada Tours program, **the final climb is offered to physically prepared participants**. This makes it possible to discuss expectations beforehand: some travelers mainly value the long day amid mountains, while others are specifically aiming to reach the shore of the glacial lake. Any route changes or alternative excursions must be agreed separately; the published description does not automatically guarantee substitutions.

## Questions about tours to Laguna de los Tres

### Is the Laguna de los Tres hike included in the Ada Tours itinerary?

**Day 8 includes a full trekking outing in this area.** The most demanding final ascent to the lake's shore is offered to those prepared for the extra effort, according to the [13-day tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/).

### Do I have to walk the full 25 km from El Chaltén?

Not necessarily. The 25 km figure refers to the standard out-and-back trail from the village. The Ada Tours program starts **near El Pilar after a transfer**, so its actual distance and duration cannot be equated with the classic version.

### Can I stop at Laguna Capri instead?

That is a shorter standalone hike, offering a different view farther from the granite peaks. The [Ada Tours program](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) already includes Laguna Capri separately on day 7. Declining the final climb on the following day should be discussed with the guide according to conditions.

### Is the route suitable for beginners?

A long mountain hike requires endurance, and the final ascent to the lagoon is physically demanding. If you are not used to walking for hours on uneven terrain, assess your fitness in advance and do not assume reaching the shore is essential in all weather.

### When is Fitz Roy most clearly visible?

Clear views depend on cloud, wind and local weather, which can change quickly. Even at the height of the southern summer, the peaks may be covered. Reaching Laguna de los Tres does not guarantee an unobstructed view of Fitz Roy.

## Laguna Esmeralda: trekking to an emerald lake near Ushuaia

Laguna Esmeralda is a mountain lake in Argentina's part of Tierra del Fuego, near [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/). Southern beech forests, peat bogs and steep Andean peaks surround the lake. The water may look greenish turquoise; its distinctive color comes from suspended minerals carried down from glacial slopes.

Travelers choose this destination for a proper hike rather than a brief stop at a viewpoint. Unlike driving tours around the island, it requires several hours on the trail and readiness for wet ground.

## Where the trail begins and how long it takes

The official trail crosses the Valle Tierra Mayor nature reserve. The trailhead is reached along national road RN 3, approximately 18 km from Ushuaia. From there, a marked walking path runs through forests, open areas and peat bogs.

The Tierra del Fuego tourism authority provides the following estimates for the standard route:

| Parameter | Guideline |
|---|---|
| Distance | 9 km round trip |
| Duration | About 5 hours |
| Difficulty | Moderate |

These figures describe the usual route, not a guaranteed time for every group. After heavy rain, in snow or with poor visibility, progress may be much slower. People who rarely hike on natural trails should assess their fitness in advance.

## How the scenery changes along the trail

### Lenga forests

The initial section crosses lenga forests, a southern beech species typical of Tierra del Fuego. In clear weather, mountain slopes are visible through the trees. Farther on, the forest alternates with more exposed wet areas, making footwear more important than camera equipment.

### Peat bogs and the wet valley

Peatlands form as plant matter accumulates in cold, wet conditions. They help retain water and play a special role in the local ecosystem. Stepping away from the trail can be dangerous and damaging to nature; follow markers and skirt deep mud along permitted routes instead of creating a new path through living groundcover.

### Emerald lake and mountains

The path eventually reveals water beneath steep slopes. Mount Ojo del Albino and its glacier lie nearby, and the surrounding peaks often retain snow. Even in summer, the exposed lakeshore can be colder than the sheltered forest.

The water's color changes with light and weather. It may appear less vividly turquoise under cloud, but the mountains and forests remain the main reward of the walk.

## Best time to go

For an ordinary hiking route, months with longer daylight are most convenient, generally October through April. In the shoulder seasons and winter, days are shorter, and snow, ice and freezing temperatures occur. A familiar summer trail may then require specialist equipment, experience and a guide.

Even in summer, Tierra del Fuego weather can change rapidly. Check current trail conditions, forecasts, wind strength and sunset time before starting. A forecast for downtown Ushuaia should not be taken as a complete description of conditions in the mountains.

## What to bring for the trek

Bring waterproof boots with good grip, windproof and waterproof outerwear, an extra warm layer, water and food for several hours. Trekking poles help on soft, slippery sections. In colder periods, additional winter equipment and skills for safe travel may be needed.

Mobile phone coverage is incomplete along the trail. Tell a guide or someone close to you about the route and planned return time. Leaving the marked trail for a shortcut is dangerous: peat bogs and streams can conceal deep, waterlogged patches.

## Laguna Esmeralda on an Ada Tours trip

On our [13-day Incredible Argentina journey](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/), a trek to Laguna Esmeralda is available as a separate option near Ushuaia. **The trek is offered on request and is not automatically included in the main package of services.** The core tour also features Tierra del Fuego excursions, Perito Moreno Glacier and Iguazú Falls.

This option suits travelers wanting to add a full hiking day to their journey. It must be coordinated with the Ushuaia schedule, length of stay, weather and fitness level.

If hiking is your main goal, also explore [Argentina adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/). For a gentler nature day, driving routes through [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/) and around Ushuaia may be preferable.

## Frequently asked questions about Laguna Esmeralda

### Do I need to be an experienced mountaineer?

Mountaineering skills are not required for the usual summer route, but it is a moderately demanding walk across wet peatlands. Winter brings more serious preparation and equipment requirements.

### How long does the walk take?

The official guideline is about 5 hours for 9 km round trip. Time varies with weather, ground conditions and group pace.

### Can I see the lagoon without hiking?

The standard route to the shore involves trekking. Tierra del Fuego offers beautiful views on driving excursions too, but those do not replace a visit to this lagoon.

## Tours to Laguna Esmeralda: combining trekking with a visit to Ushuaia

**[Laguna Esmeralda](/argentina/place/laguna-esmeralda/)** is a mountain lake near [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), visited for the walk through Tierra del Fuego forests and views of water surrounded by the Andes. It mainly appeals to travelers who want to spend part of their trip on foot. The mere presence of Ushuaia on an itinerary does not mean the group will hike to the lagoon.

Our selection lists {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} where Laguna Esmeralda appears among the destinations. **Check which activities are included in the paid main itinerary and which are additional excursions.** This matters especially on busy multi-day trips with flights: trekking requires its own time allowance.

## How the lagoon features in the current Ada Tours itinerary

The [13-day Incredible Argentina: Buenos Aires, Ushuaia, El Calafate and Iguazú tour](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/) combines the capital, Tierra del Fuego, glacial Patagonia and Iguazú Falls on both sides of the border. During the Ushuaia part, the program lists a separate [Laguna Esmeralda trekking excursion](/argentina/ushuaia/laguna-esmeralda-hike-from-ushuaia/). **Trekking is marked as optional**, so its price and position in the schedule must be considered separately from activities already included.

The main itinerary includes flying from Buenos Aires to Ushuaia, followed by a visit to [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/), a boat trip along the [Beagle Channel](/argentina/place/beagle-channel/) and an off-road journey to the island's lakes. After Ushuaia, the journey continues to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). Choosing the trek therefore means dividing time and energy among several different activities.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_neveroyatnaya_argentina}}

If a mountain walk and a relaxed stop beside the lagoon matter most, arrange extra time in Ushuaia in advance. If you want to see more of Argentina in a single journey, the 13-day route covers extensive geography but has a fuller schedule.

## How long the hike takes

According to Ushuaia's tourism department, **the main path is approximately 9 km round trip**, with an elevation change of around 220 m. Walking takes roughly **4–5 hours**. The trail begins near national road No. 3, about 18 km from Ushuaia. Transfer time, preparations and stops add to the duration of the hike itself.

The path crosses southern beech lenga forest and open peatlands. Shoes quickly get wet on damp stretches, while the wind is stronger in open areas. It cannot be considered an easy city stroll, although it requires no mountaineering or technical climbing.

Ada Tours' standalone excursion describes a route through subantarctic forest, peat valleys and areas with beaver dams, a stop beside the lake and a return along the same trail. Its own services include a packed lunch and a hot drink. These are terms of **that specific excursion**, not benefits automatically included in every tour through Ushuaia.

## How the hike differs from other Tierra del Fuego days

| Experience | What you do |
|---|---|
| [Laguna Esmeralda](/argentina/place/laguna-esmeralda/) | Walk through forest and peat bogs to a mountain lake |
| [Tierra del Fuego](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/) | Explore coastal landscapes, bays and national park trails |
| [Beagle Channel](/argentina/place/beagle-channel/) | Observe coasts and islands from the water |
| [Lake Escondido](/argentina/place/lake-escondido-tierra-del-fuego/) | Drive to lake valleys, sometimes with 4×4 sections |

All these activities are on the same island, but they differ in exertion and transportation. For example, the published visit to Lake Escondido uses off-road vehicles and a short walking section. At Esmeralda, the central activity is a several-hour hike.

If combining several nature experiences, first decide which days involve long walks. A trekking day is best planned without another mandatory hike of similar length.

## When to go and how to prepare

Weather near Ushuaia can change within a few hours, and much of the trail is wet. The Southern Hemisphere's summer months are generally more suitable for hiking because daylight lasts longer, but a waterproof jacket, warm layer and grippy shoes are needed even in summer. Winter snow and ice change conditions: some sections may require specialized equipment and guiding.

The city tourism office recommends selecting a suitable trail by **two separate criteria**: terrain difficulty and physical effort. Esmeralda has a relatively modest elevation gain, but the wet ground, wind and duration make preparation important. Before departure, check the forecast, trail conditions and whether you can return in daylight. A specialist guide improves safety.

For a trip with several domestic flights, weather allowances are particularly important. If a flight lands late, attempting a full hike on arrival day is risky. Discuss a separate date or itinerary change before confirming the trip.

## Choosing the right format

If you want to experience [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), glaciers, Iguazú and Buenos Aires in one journey, start with the published [13-day route](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/). Then decide where to spend an extra day: trekking to Esmeralda, visiting Tierra del Fuego's lakes or staying longer in El Calafate.

If the lagoon is your main goal, make the separate [trek from Ushuaia](/argentina/ushuaia/laguna-esmeralda-hike-from-ushuaia/) a required part of your individually agreed itinerary. Compare walking time, seasonal access and the time remaining for other activities. The general [Argentina tour selection](/argentina/tour/) can help you consider shorter or differently arranged routes.

## Questions about tours to Laguna Esmeralda

### Is Laguna Esmeralda included in the 13-day tour price?

On the [13-day tour](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/), the hike is listed as a separate **optional excursion**. Its terms and price are in the [trek description](/argentina/ushuaia/laguna-esmeralda-hike-from-ushuaia/); the lagoon's mention does not automatically add this service to the tour's base price.

### How much time should I allow?

The walking portion usually takes around **4–5 hours** over approximately **9 km round trip**. Add the drive from Ushuaia and preparation time. In practice, this takes a distinct part of the day.

### Can I see the lagoon without a long walk?

The main way to reach its shore is by trail. Visiting Esmeralda cannot be replaced by a brief bus stop at a viewpoint. For natural scenery with less walking, consider other Tierra del Fuego excursions, such as lake drives.

### Which is better: Laguna Esmeralda or Lake Escondido?

Travelers visit Esmeralda for a [walking route](/argentina/ushuaia/laguna-esmeralda-hike-from-ushuaia/), while [Lake Escondido](/argentina/place/lake-escondido-tierra-del-fuego/) is more often reached on a mountain-road drive or a 4×4 tour. Walking demands of the latter depend on the specific excursion.

### Is a guide necessary for the trek?

Ushuaia's tourism office recommends specialized agencies for safety. This is especially important in snow, poor visibility, wind and when you lack experience of wet mountain trails.
